_comment: West Virginia 2025 and 2026 Allocation Plan, West Virginia Housing Development Fund. Page numbers are PDF page indices; the printed 'Page N' runs twelve lower. The p.30 summary states TOTAL POINTS AVAILABLE 993 for both New Supply and Existing Low-Income Housing, which score the same criteria at different values. TWO FULL PARALLEL TRACKS: New Supply is the default track and Existing Low-Income Housing is track 'existing'. Every criterion that applies to both appears twice, with a '.E' suffix on the Existing copy, so that each universe reconciles on its own. It is one criterion in the document, not two. Section totals checked against p.30, New Supply / Existing: Property Characteristics 120 / 235; Ability to Produce 180 / 180; Location and Housing Needs 200 / 100; Sponsor 3; Tenant Populations 20; PHA Waiting List 25; Tenant Ownership 5; Historic 20; Lowest Income 50; Longest Periods 150; QCT/CRP 35; Energy and Quality 185 / 170; total 993 / 993. MISMATCH BY DESIGN: Tenant Ownership (5) and Longest Periods (150) bar each other (pp.73, 76), so the reachable maximum is 988 on each track. The 993 counts both. Family/senior un-met need and school/senior amenities are alternatives within their sections, and the section maxima count them once. A 10-point Top Off bonus (track top_off_bonus) and negative points sit outside the 993. Minimum 500 (p.30). Mixed properties are scored on a unit-weighted average of the two tracks.

track_totals.note: New Supply. TOTAL POINTS AVAILABLE 993. Computed 988: Tenant Ownership (5) and Longest Periods (150) are mutually exclusive but both are in the 993. MISMATCH by design, fully explained.
Existing Low-Income Housing. 993 stated, 988 computed, for the same reason.
10 bonus points for a Top Off applicant in its final permitted year, beyond the 993.
